segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. Whether it's Cinderella, David and Goliath or the Rocky movies,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: we all love an underdog story. The underdog in a situation is the person who seems least

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: likely to win. Nevertheless, with some luck and plenty of hard work, the underdog sometimes

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: ends up the winner.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sport is full of underdog stories

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: minor teams and sports people who play with courage

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and end up beating the superstars and multi-million pound clubs.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But if you were given a choice between your team being the favourite to win

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or being the underdog, it's pretty obvious you'd want to be the favourite, right?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, yes, being the favourite gives a team confidence.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But maybe the fact that no one expects the underdog to win

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: is actually an advantage which could help them to a surprise victory.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: In this programme, we'll be hearing about an underdog football club doing just that.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary too.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Great, but first I have a question for you, Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: One of the biggest underdog stories in sports history

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: happened in the 2015-16 English football season

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: when a little-known club beat top clubs like Manchester City and Liverpool

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: overcoming odds of 5 to 1 to win the Premier League But which club was it A Charlton Athletic B Leicester City or C Crystal Palace

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'll guess it was Crystal Palace.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, Georgie, I'll reveal the correct answer at the end of the programme.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The English Football Premier League is a good place to find underdogs.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Each season, the three best clubs in the second league are promoted up.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: while the three weakest Premier League clubs are relegated down.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: One club that knows all about relegation is Luton Town FC.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: In 2009, Luton Town were relegated entirely from the English League.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Slowly their fortunes improved, however,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and they've now become the first English team to progress from non-league to the Premier League.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Here's Luton fan Alex talking about his team's chances to BBC radio programme Mental Muscle.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But some of these elite Premier League clubs will look down their nose at us and just think we shouldn't be there

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and we are there on merit and we've just got to prove it this season.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So we are the underdog, certainly financially, but on the pitch I don't think we will be.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Alex thinks some of the rich Premier League clubs look down their noses at Luton.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you look down your nose at someone, you think you're better than them.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But underdogs Luton have done better than expected,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: even beating some of the big clubs like Newcastle United.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: The question is how Is there something about being the underdog that improves a team chances of winning To answer that sports psychologist Gillian Cook spoke to BBC radio programme Mental Muscle So you can find that when the newly promoted

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: team comes up, they've got high confidence because they've just come from a season of winning. So

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: they've got the belief that they can do it. But on the flip side, it's just as important to look at

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: the top dog's performance, who everyone expects them to win. They're playing the newly promoted

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: teams. We might think of Mad City, who might be about to come up against a Luton town. So what we

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: can see from that is what in psychology literature is known as choking, and that's when pressure gets

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: to an individual or a team and they underperform.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Clubs newly promoted to the Premier League are

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: used to winning and start the season confidently. On the flip side, they have to play much stronger

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: teams than before. The phrase on the flip side is used to show the opposite, less positive side of

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Of course, it's not just the underdog playing, there are also top dogs, the most successful or powerful person or team.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No one expects underdogs to win and this gives them freedom to relax and play naturally.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Top dogs, on the other hand, experience a lot of expectation and this sometimes leads to choking,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: a sports term which describes the failure of a player to perform their best because of psychological pressure or social expectation.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Choking causes teams and players to underperform to perform worse than expected It also true that neutral fans people watching a match when their team isn playing tend to support the underdog as well In football it tough at the top

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think it's time to reveal the answer to your question, Neil. You asked me about the

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: famous Premier League winning underdogs of the 2015-16 football season, and I guessed

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: it was Crystal Palace.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Which was the wrong answer, I'm afraid, Georgie. In fact, it was Leicester City, nicknamed the Foxes, who became the unexpected champions of the Premier League.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned from this programme about the underdog, the person in a competition or situation who seems least likely to win.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you look down your nose at someone, you think you are superior to them.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The phrase on the flip side is used to show the opposite, less positive or less popular side of something.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: The top dog is an informal way of saying the most successful or powerful person in a group.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: In sports, choking happens when a player or team fail to perform their best because of psychological pressure or social expectation.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And finally, the verb to underperform means to perform worse than expected.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Once again, our six minutes are up.

segments.speaker: Georgie
